        to another folder clears the selection and scrolls back to the top.

    choosing:
        The footer shows the folder that will be chosen: the selected folder,
        or the current folder when none is selected. "Choose" chooses it and
        "Cancel" leaves without choosing.

shape NewProjectShape:
    description:
        A form titled "New Project", with a close button, holding the project's

        "Cancel" button and a primary "New" button that creates it. The name
        field has focus when the form opens.

    name:
        A "Name" field for the project's name, which is also the name of its
        folder. It can't be empty, contain a slash or backslash, or be "." or
        "..".

    location:
        A "Location" row showing the folder the project's folder goes in, with a
        "Browse…" button beside it. It starts in the folder holding the open
        project, or the user's home folder when no project is open. Beneath it,
        muted, the full path of the folder that will be created.

        Browse opens a @{FolderBrowserScope} in place of the form, titled
        "Choose where the project goes" and starting in the current location.
        Choosing a folder makes it the location, and choosing or cancelling
        goes back to the form, just as it was left.

    agents:
        An "Agents" group of checkboxes, one per agent Belay writes for, each
        with the directory it writes into: "Claude Code" (.claude), "OpenCode"
        (.opencode), "Codex" (.codex), "Cursor" (.cursor), and "Agents"
        (.agents). Only Claude Code starts checked. At least one must be
        checked.

    folders:
        Three fields, each a path relative to the project folder: "Spec root",
        starting as ./spec; "Code root", starting as ./src; and "Shape root",
        starting as ./spec/shape, which can be left empty to go without one.
        Spec root and code root can't be empty. A path is written with a
        leading ./ whether or not it was typed with one, and none can be
        absolute or climb out of the project with "..".

    config:
        The piton.config.pi written for the project uses @piton/config and
        @piton/belay. It exports a piton-config anchor named after the project,
        its name in PascalCase from its letters and digits, or "Project" when
        that leaves nothing or starts with a digit, whose root is the spec root,
        whose entry is index.pi in the spec root, and whose only framework is a
        belay-config anchor named BelayConfiguration. That anchor has the code
        root as its codeRoot, the shape root as its shapeRoot unless there is
        none, and an adapter for each checked agent, in the order they are
        listed. Claude Code and OpenCode use ClaudeAdapter and OpenCodeAdapter,
        imported from @piton/belay; each of the others is a belay-agent-adapter
        anchor of its own written into the file, named after the agent, such as
        CodexAdapter, with a description saying the directory it writes into
        and its tool's flag set to true. The file is written in Piton's
        canonical formatting.

    creating:
        "New" is disabled, with a tooltip saying why, until the name is valid,
        the paths are, and an agent is checked, and while a project is being
        created. A field that isn't valid says why beneath it once something has
        been typed in it.

        Pressing it creates the project's folder, and any folders leading to it,
        then writes piton.config.pi there, creates the spec root with an empty
        index.pi in it, and creates the code root and any shape root. It never
        overwrites anything: a folder that already holds a piton.config.pi is
        refused, an index.pi already in the spec root is left as it is, and
        folders that already exist are kept. Once created, the project opens as
        if picked through the @{ProjectDirectoryScope}, and the form closes. If
        anything fails, the form stays open and says what went wrong above its
        buttons.
EOF

There's now a New Project button on the Project tab. It opens a form in the same inset panel as the diff view. You set the project's name, location and Belay options, press New, and it writes `piton.config.pi`, creates the folders and opens the project. I haven't looked at the form in the running app yet, so the layout and looks are untested.

**The form:**
- **Name:** also becomes the project's folder name. It can't be empty, contain a slash, or be `.` or `..`.
- **Location:** starts in the folder that holds the current project, or your home folder. The full path to be created shows underneath. "Browse…" opens the folder browser.

- **New:** disabled until everything is valid, and its tooltip says what's missing. Invalid fields say why underneath.

**What pressing New does:**
- **Config:** writes a `piton.config.pi` in the same shape as this repo's, with `piton format` applied. The top-level anchor is named after the project, e.g. "my-app" becomes `MyApp`. Claude and OpenCode use the adapters `@piton/belay` provides. Codex, Cursor and Agents have no ready-made adapter, so the file defines its own small adapter for each. I checked that `piton build` accepts this.
- **Folders:** creates the spec root with an empty `index.pi`, plus the code and shape roots.
- **Nothing is overwritten:** a folder that already has a `piton.config.pi` is refused, and an existing `index.pi` is kept.
- **Opening:** the project opens and the panel closes. If something fails, the form stays open and shows the error.

**Folder browser:** built in the app with no new crates, not the system file dialog. It has up and home buttons, a clickable breadcrumb of the path, and a "Show hidden" checkbox.
